components.note: 土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'
雨 (rain) — 震 originally described thunder shaking the sky along with a storm.
辰 (chén) gives a sound distantly related to zhèn, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 这次地震摧毁了许多房屋。
example.pinyin: zhè cì dìzhèn cuīhuǐle xǔduō fángwū.
example.english: This earthquake destroyed many houses.
example.fact: The 1960 Great Chilean Earthquake, magnitude 9.5, is the most powerful earthquake ever recorded by modern seismographs; it triggered a Pacific-wide tsunami that killed people as far away as Japan and Hawaii, some 22 hours after the quake struck. Seismologists still use it as the benchmark for calibrating the moment magnitude scale.

components.note: 才 depicts a young sprout just breaking through the soil — new growth came to represent budding talent or ability.
十 (ten, suggesting abundance) — relates to 华's meaning 'flowery, splendid,' an abundance of blossoms.
化 (huà) gives a sound hint — 华 is pronounced huá, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 她的才华让所有人都很惊讶。
example.pinyin: tā de cáihuá ràng suǒyǒu rén dōu hěn jīngyà.
example.english: Her talent surprised everyone.
example.fact: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart composed his first symphony at age eight and had already toured European royal courts as a performing prodigy by then; modern researchers who studied his manuscripts found strikingly few corrections, suggesting he often composed complete pieces in his head before writing them down.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 机 originally referred to a wooden device or machine, such as a loom.
几 depicts a small table or stool — combined with 木 (wood), the character pictured a wooden machine or mechanism.
覀 here depicts rising flames.
示 (altar) — burning paper offerings over an altar, a traditional practice, gave 票 its meaning of a paper note, later 'ticket, banknote.'

example.hanzi: 我已经订好了去北京的机票。
example.pinyin: wǒ yǐjīng dìnghǎole qù Běijīng de jīpiào.
example.english: I have already booked the plane ticket to Beijing.
example.fact: Airline ticket prices fluctuate constantly because of "revenue management" software, first pioneered by American Airlines in the 1980s, which reprices seats based on demand, booking patterns, and how many days remain before departure. The same seat can sell for wildly different prices within a single day.

components.note: 日 (sun) — represents the sun.
十 depicts the first rays of sunlight appearing low on the horizon — together with 日 (sun) giving 早 its meaning 'early, morning.'
饣 (food) — 饭 names cooked rice, a meal.
反 (fǎn) gives the sound — an exact match with 饭.

example.hanzi: 他每天早上七点吃早饭。
example.pinyin: tā měitiān zǎoshang qī diǎn chī zǎofàn.
example.english: He eats breakfast at seven every morning.
example.fact: The word "breakfast" simply means breaking the overnight fast, but the modern idea of it as the day's most important meal was heavily promoted by cereal companies like Kellogg's in the early 20th century as part of marketing campaigns. Nutrition scientists today are far more divided on the claim than the slogan suggests.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 情 relates to feelings and emotions.
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 情 is pronounced qíng, a close match differing only in tone.
节 is the simplified form of 節, which depicted the segmented sections of a bamboo stalk ⺮ — giving 节 its meaning 'joint, section, festival.'

example.hanzi: 这部电影的情节非常复杂。
example.pinyin: zhè bù diànyǐng de qíngjié fēicháng fùzá.
example.english: This movie's plot is very complicated.
example.fact: The three-act story structure, still the backbone of most films today, was formally popularized by screenwriting teacher Syd Field in his 1979 book "Screenplay," though the underlying pattern of setup, confrontation, and resolution traces back to Aristotle's "Poetics," written more than two thousand years earlier.

components.note: 王 (jade, written without its dot) — 玩 originally meant to handle and admire a piece of jade, extending to 'to play, to have fun.'
元 (yuán) gives a sound distantly related to wán, having drifted apart over time.
儿 (simplified from 兒) depicts a small child, drawn with a large head on a small body — a simple picture of youth.

example.hanzi: 孩子们喜欢在公园里玩儿。
example.pinyin: háizimen xǐhuan zài gōngyuán lǐ wánr.
example.english: Children love to play in the park.
example.fact: Play is not unique to humans. Young octopuses have been observed repeatedly bouncing a floating pill bottle back and forth using their water jets in what researchers concluded was true play behavior, since it served no survival purpose and the octopuses appeared to enjoy the repetition.

meanings: policeman (general term for any police officer)

components.note: 言 (speech) — 警 relates to speaking out a warning or alarm
敬 (jìng) gives a sound close to 警's reading jǐng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
贝 (shell/money — cowrie shells were historically used as currency) — 员 originally related to counting or officials responsible for accounts, later broadening to mean 'member' or 'personnel.'

example.hanzi: 一名警员在路口指挥交通。
example.pinyin: yī míng jǐngyuán zài lùkǒu zhǐhuī jiāotōng.
example.english: A police officer is directing traffic at the intersection.
example.fact: London's Metropolitan Police, founded in 1829 by Sir Robert Peel, is considered the first modern police force. Officers were deliberately unarmed and wore blue rather than red to avoid resembling the military, an approach that still shapes British policing culture today.

components.note: 车 (cart) — relates to 转's meaning 'to turn, change direction,' like a wheel turning.
专 (zhuān) gives a sound hint — 转 is pronounced zhuǎn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

变 is the simplified form of 變, whose traditional structure combined 言 (speech) with 攴 (a hand holding a tool) — the idea of altering something through repeated action and effort gave 变 its meaning 'to change, to transform.'

example.hanzi: 他的态度发生了很大的转变。
example.pinyin: tā de tàidù fāshēngle hěn dà de zhuǎnbiàn.
example.english: His attitude underwent a great transformation.
example.fact: The monarch butterfly's transformation from caterpillar to adult is one of nature's most extreme metamorphoses. Inside the chrysalis, the caterpillar's body largely dissolves into a nutrient-rich soup called a histolysate, from which entirely new structures like wings are built using clusters of cells called imaginal discs.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 操 relates to controlling or handling something.
喿 (zào) gives a sound distantly related to cāo, having drifted apart over time.
亻 (person) plus 乍 (suddenly/for the first time) — together suggesting a person making or doing something for the first time.

example.hanzi: 请按照说明操作这台机器。
example.pinyin: qǐng ànzhào shuōmíng cāozuò zhè tái jīqì.
example.english: Please operate this machine according to the instructions.
example.fact: The first industrial robot, Unimate, went to work on a General Motors assembly line in 1961, lifting and stacking hot pieces of die-cast metal, a task considered too dangerous for human workers. Its success helped launch the global industrial automation industry.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 最 pictures something happening under the sun, that is, everywhere.
取 (to take, gather) — combined with the sun above, gathering everything under the sun gave 最 its meaning of 'most' or 'the utmost.'
衤 (clothing) — the cloth that is about to be cut
刀 (a knife) — cutting the cloth is the first step in making clothes

example.hanzi: 我最初并不喜欢这个想法。
example.pinyin: wǒ zuìchū bìng bù xǐhuan zhège xiǎngfǎ.
example.english: I didn't like this idea at first.
example.fact: The first photograph ever taken of a person was captured by Louis Daguerre in 1838 on a Paris boulevard. Because his exposure took several minutes, the moving crowd vanished from the image entirely, leaving only a man who stood still long enough getting his boots polished, the earliest known photo of a human being.

components.note: 匕 (a kneeling person) — a mourner bowed down in grief.
歹 (skeletal remains) — the corpse being mourned, the source of 死's meaning 'to die, dead.'

囗 (an enclosure) surrounding 大 (a person) — the character originally pictured a person resting on a mat inside a room, relying on it for support, which extended to 因's meaning 'cause, reason, because of.'

example.hanzi: 警方还在调查他的死因。
example.pinyin: jǐngfāng hái zài diàochá tā de sǐyīn.
example.english: The police are still investigating his cause of death.
example.fact: Forensic pathologists determine cause of death using an autopsy protocol largely standardized in the mid-20th century. One enduring puzzle in the field is "excited delirium," a controversial term used to explain sudden deaths during police restraint, which several major medical associations have since disavowed as lacking scientific basis.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 组 originally meant 'to weave, arrange,' extended to 'group, to organize.'
且 (qiě) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from zǔ.

成 traces back to an ancient pictograph of a halberd-like weapon with an added mark showing a finished strike — the idea of an action carried through to completion gave 成 its meaning 'to become, to complete, to succeed.'

example.hanzi: 委员会由五名成员组成。
example.pinyin: wěiyuánhuì yóu wǔ míng chéngyuán zǔchéng.
example.english: The committee is formed by five members.
example.fact: Water is made of just two elements, hydrogen and oxygen, yet the specific way those atoms bond, an angle of about 104.5 degrees, gives water a slight electric polarity that lets it dissolve more substances than almost any other liquid. That's why chemists call it the "universal solvent."

components.note: 夂 (a foot, to walk) — 各 pictures people arriving from different directions.
口 (mouth) — different people speaking gave 各 its meaning 'each' or 'every,' emphasizing individual distinctness.
A picture of a nose; because people in ancient China would point to their own nose when referring to themselves, the character came to mean 'self.'

example.hanzi: 大家各自回到了自己的房间。
example.pinyin: dàjiā gèzì huí dàole zìjǐ de fángjiān.
example.english: Everyone returned to their own respective rooms.
example.fact: Honeybee colonies divide labor so precisely that biologists describe each bee as performing its own respective role: nurse, forager, guard, or undertaker. A bee's job typically changes with age, shifting from indoor nursing duties as a young bee to outdoor foraging once it's older and its wings are more worn.

components.note: 弋 (a dagger-axe/weapon) — represents military force.
止 (foot/to stop) — stopping an enemy by force of arms gave 武 its meaning 'military, martial.'

士 pictured an axe-like tool, symbolizing someone capable of performing skilled tasks. Over time its meaning broadened from a person skilled with tools to a wider term for a capable man — a scholar, gentleman, or soldier.

example.hanzi: 那个武士拿着一把长剑。
example.pinyin: nàge wǔshì zhezhe yī bǎ cháng jiàn.
example.english: That warrior carries a long sword.
example.fact: Japanese samurai swords, or katana, were traditionally forged by folding the steel repeatedly, sometimes over a dozen times, to remove impurities and create thousands of microscopic layers. The technique also produced the wavy hardening pattern called hamon visible along the blade's edge.

components.note: 壴 (a drum) — beating a drum in celebration
口 (mouth) — singing along in celebration
冖 (a roof/house) — the home being welcomed into.
友 (a friend) — brought close into one's home; the traditional form 愛 also includes 心 ('heart') in the middle — the source of 爱's meaning 'to love.'

example.hanzi: 我特别喜爱中国的传统文化。
example.pinyin: wǒ tèbié xǐ'ài Zhōngguó de chuántǒng wénhuà.
example.english: I especially like traditional Chinese culture.
example.fact: Psychologists have found that mere repeated exposure to something, a song, a face, even an abstract shape, tends to increase how much people like it. This phenomenon, called the "mere-exposure effect," was first documented experimentally by Robert Zajonc in 1968.

components.note: A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
体 is the simplified form of 體, combining 亻 (person) with 本 (root, foundation) — the body pictured as the physical foundation a person is built on, giving 体 its meaning 'body.'

example.hanzi: 这本书详细介绍了人体的结构。
example.pinyin: zhè běn shū xiángxì jièshàole réntǐ de jiégòu.
example.english: This book introduces the structure of the human body in detail.
example.fact: The human body contains roughly 37 trillion cells, but it also hosts an even larger number of bacteria, fungi, and other microbes, collectively called the microbiome, living mostly in the gut. Research increasingly links this microbial community to digestion, immunity, and even mood.

components.note: 专 is the simplified form of 專, which originally pictured a spinning spindle turned steadily by hand — that single, unwavering motion gave 专 its meaning 'specialized, concentrated, exclusive.'
心 was originally a pictograph of the physical shape of a human heart, and came to represent the mind, feelings, and intention as well.

example.hanzi: 学习的时候要专心。
example.pinyin: xuéxí de shíhou yào zhuānxīn.
example.english: You need to focus when studying.
example.fact: Cognitive scientists have shown that what feels like "multitasking" is usually just rapid switching between tasks, and each switch carries a measurable cost. Studies estimate it can take over 20 minutes to fully regain deep focus after a single interruption, which is why sustained, single-task concentration is so valuable for complex work.

components.note: Door — a screen is a barrier like a door.
Gives the sound bìng, related to píng but drifted apart over time.
巾 (cloth) — 幕 names a large piece of cloth, a curtain or screen.
莫 (mò) gives a sound close to mù, sharing the same rhyme.

example.hanzi: 请把手机屏幕的亮度调低一点。
example.pinyin: qǐng bǎ shǒujī píngmù de liàngdù tiáo dī yīdiǎn.
example.english: Please turn down the brightness of the phone screen a bit.
example.fact: The first LCD screens were developed in the late 1960s at RCA's research labs, but it took until the 1980s for the technology to become efficient and affordable enough for everyday devices like calculators and laptops. Decades of engineering separated the original lab discovery from the screens now used constantly.

meanings: to visit (a place, e.g. museum or factory)

components.note: 彡 (shān) is the historical phonetic component of 参; sound change over time has left little resemblance to the modern reading cān
见 (to see) — the act of looking.
又 (again, or a hand) — looking closely or repeatedly, giving 观 its meaning 'to observe, view.'

example.hanzi: 我们下周要去参观博物馆。
example.pinyin: wǒmen xià zhōu yào qù cānguān bówùguǎn.
example.english: We are going to visit the museum next week.
example.fact: The Louvre in Paris, the world's most visited museum, welcomes roughly 30,000 visitors a day when at capacity, and the Mona Lisa alone draws such dense crowds that the museum installed a dedicated bulletproof glass enclosure and rerouted foot traffic just to manage the flow of people trying to see it.

components.note: 杰 combines 木 (tree) with 灬 (fire) — the image of a tall tree standing out above a blaze evokes someone who rises above the rest, giving 杰 its meaning 'outstanding, heroic.'
大 (a grown man) — the figure being depicted.
一 (a hairpin) — worn across the top of the head to mark a coming-of-age ceremony, giving 夫 its meaning 'man, husband.'

example.hanzi: 杰夫昨天搬到了新公司上班。
example.pinyin: Jiéfū zuótiān bāndàole xīn gōngsī shàngbān.
example.english: Jeff moved to a new company to work yesterday.
example.fact: The name Jeffrey derives from the Old French "Geoffroi," itself likely rooted in Germanic elements meaning "district" or "peace," and it entered English usage after the Norman Conquest of 1066, when Norman French names largely displaced older Anglo-Saxon naming conventions among the English nobility.

components.note: A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
米 (grain) — 番 pictures seeds scattered by hand.
田 (a farm field) — seeds 米 sown onto a field 田 gave 番 its meaning 'a turn, a time' — as one crop follows another in turn.

example.hanzi: 他把整个房间打扫了一番。
example.pinyin: tā bǎ zhěnggè fángjiān dǎsǎole yī fān.
example.english: He gave the whole room a thorough cleaning.
example.fact: The measure-word idea behind phrases like this echoes how English uses expressions such as "a round of applause." Many languages have specialized counting words for actions rather than objects, which linguists call "verbal classifiers," and Chinese has an unusually rich system of them for describing everything from glances to conversations.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 演 originally described water flowing and spreading out, later extended to 'developing, unfolding'
寅 (yín) gives a sound distantly related to 演's reading yǎn, having drifted apart over time
口 (mouth) — 唱 describes singing, an action made with the mouth.
昌 (chāng) gives a sound close to chàng, differing only in tone.
人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'

example.hanzi: 昨晚的演唱会太精彩了。
example.pinyin: zuówǎn de yǎnchànghuì tài jīngcǎile.
example.english: Last night's concert was amazing.
example.fact: The largest paid attendance ever recorded for a single concert was Rod Stewart's 1994 New Year's Eve show on Copacabana Beach in Rio de Janeiro, which drew an estimated 3.5 million people. That crowd remains listed in Guinness World Records as the biggest concert audience in history.

components.note: 木 (wood) — early spears and rifle stocks were made of wood.
仓 (cāng) gives a sound close to qiāng, sharing the same rhyme.
乂 depicts crossed strokes suggesting a cutting action.
木 (wood) here represents a wooden stake — giving 杀 its meaning 'to kill.'

example.hanzi: 那名嫌疑人被警方枪杀。
example.pinyin: nà míng xiányírén bèi jǐngfāng qiāngshā.
example.english: The suspect was shot dead by the police.
example.fact: Ballistics experts can often trace a bullet back to a specific firearm because the barrel's rifling, spiral grooves that spin the bullet for accuracy, leaves microscopic scratches unique to that individual gun. This forensic technique was first used successfully in a criminal case in the 1920s.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — the act of speaking.
牛 (ox) — traditionally read as speaking with the forceful weight of an ox, giving 告 its meaning 'to tell, announce, inform.'
另 (other, separate) — 别 relates to distinguishing one thing from another.
刂 (knife) — cutting things apart to sort them gave 别 its meaning 'to separate' or 'other,' and later, 'don't' as a command.

example.hanzi: 我们在机场向他告别。
example.pinyin: wǒmen zài jīchǎng xiàng tā gàobié.
example.english: We said goodbye to him at the airport.
example.fact: The custom of waving goodbye may trace back to ancient gestures of showing an open, empty hand to prove one held no weapon. Anthropologists note that similar open-palm greeting and farewell gestures appear independently across many unrelated cultures worldwide.

components.note: 木 (tree) — traditionally read as a tree that has borne fruit.
立 (standing) — standing close by to watch it grow, evoking closeness and nurture, extended to 亲's meaning 'close, dear; parent, relative.'
口 (mouth) — kissing is done with the mouth.
勿 (wù) gives a sound distantly related to wěn, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 母亲亲吻了孩子的额头。
example.pinyin: mǔqīn qīnwěnle háizi de étóu.
example.english: The mother kissed the child's forehead.
example.fact: Not all cultures practice romantic kissing. A 2015 cross-cultural survey found that fewer than half of the 168 societies studied showed any evidence of romantic-sexual kissing, suggesting it is a widespread but far from universal human custom rather than an innate behavior.

components.note: 贝 (money, valuables) shows 贡 relates to goods offered up.
工 (gōng) gives a sound close to gòng, sharing the initial consonant though the tone differs.
犬 (dog) — 献 originally referred to offering a dog in sacrifice, extended to mean 'to offer, present.'
南 (nán) gives a sound distantly related to xiàn, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他为公司的发展做出了巨大贡献。
example.pinyin: tā wèi gōngsī de fāzhǎn zuòchūle jùdà gòngxiàn.
example.english: He made a huge contribution to the company's development.
example.fact: Norman Borlaug, an agricultural scientist, is credited with contributions that saved an estimated one billion lives by breeding high-yield, disease-resistant wheat varieties during the mid-20th century "Green Revolution." He received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970 for that work.

components.note: 土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'
亻 (person) — 位 relates to a person's location.
立 (to stand) — the spot where a person stands gave 位 its meaning 'position' or 'place,' and later, a polite measure word for people.

example.hanzi: 她在公司里有很高的地位。
example.pinyin: tā zài gōngsī lǐ yǒu hěn gāo de dìwèi.
example.english: She holds a high status in the company.
example.fact: In naked mole-rat colonies, social status is enforced almost entirely by the queen, the colony's sole breeding female, who maintains her position partly through physical shoving of subordinates. Researchers have found her vertebrae actually lengthen after she takes power, letting her grow larger to reinforce her dominant status.

components.note: 王 (jade) — 琼 describes a fine, precious kind of jade.
京 (jīng) gives a sound distantly related to 琼's reading qióng, having drifted apart over time.

斯 combines 其 (a winnowing basket) with 斤 (an axe) — using an axe to split something apart gave 斯 its original meaning 'to split,' though today it mostly serves as a sound-transliteration character in names and loanwords.

example.hanzi: 琼斯先生是我们的新老师。
example.pinyin: Qióngsī xiānsheng shì wǒmen de xīn lǎoshī.
example.english: Mr. Jones is our new teacher.
example.fact: "Jones" is one of the most common surnames in Wales, originating as a patronymic meaning "son of John." Because John was such a widespread given name in medieval Britain, Jones became disproportionately common in Welsh-speaking regions compared to the rest of the United Kingdom.

meanings: to feel a twinge of guilt

components.note: 冂 (an enclosure or doorway) — 内 pictures the space one enters.
人 (person) — a person entering an enclosure gave 内 its meaning 'inside' or 'within.'
疒 (sickness) — the sickness radical, depicting a person lying on a sickbed — marking the character as related to illness.
久 (jiǔ) gives a sound close to 疚's reading jiù — the same syllable, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 他因为说了谎而感到内疚。
example.pinyin: tā yīnwèi shuōle huǎng ér gǎndào nèijiù.
example.english: He felt guilty for having lied.
example.fact: Neuroscientists have found that feelings of guilt activate the same brain regions involved in physical pain processing, including the anterior insula. That is one reason researchers describe emotional guilt as genuinely "hurting" rather than being purely metaphorical.

components.note: 辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 运's meaning 'to move, transport,' and by extension 'fortune,' the movement of one's life.
云 (yún) gives a sound hint — 运 is pronounced yùn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
亻 (person) plus 乍 (suddenly/for the first time) — together suggesting a person making or doing something for the first time.

example.hanzi: 这个系统运作得很稳定。
example.pinyin: zhège xìtǒng yùnzuò de hěn wěndìng.
example.english: This system operates very stably.
example.fact: The New York City subway operates around the clock, 24 hours a day, every day of the year, one of only a handful of major transit systems in the world that never fully shuts down for overnight maintenance. That forces crews to service tracks and trains while trains are still running on other lines.

components.note: The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
禾 (grain, a growing rice or wheat plant) — 利 pictures a harvest.
刂 (knife) — cutting grain at harvest time was a clear benefit or gain, giving 利 its meaning 'profit' or 'advantage.'

example.hanzi: 天气对比赛非常不利。
example.pinyin: tiānqì duì bǐsài fēicháng bùlì.
example.english: The weather is very unfavorable for the match.
example.fact: Home-field advantage in professional sports is measurable and real. Statisticians analyzing decades of soccer, basketball, and baseball results consistently find home teams win 55 to 60 percent of games, an edge researchers attribute to crowd noise affecting referee decisions as well as travel fatigue for the away side.

components.note: 氵 (water) — the water that is deep.
罙 (deep) — combined with water, giving 深 its meaning 'deep.'
夂 (a foot, to go) — 处 relates to arriving somewhere.
卜 (a mark or flag) — planting a marker after arriving gave 处 its meaning of 'a place' or 'to settle, deal with.'

example.hanzi: 潜水员潜入了海洋深处。
example.pinyin: qiánshuǐyuán qiánrùle hǎiyáng shēnchù.
example.english: The diver dove into the depths of the ocean.
example.fact: The deepest point in the ocean, the Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench, lies nearly 11,000 meters below the surface, deep enough that if Mount Everest were placed at its bottom, the peak would still sit over 2,000 meters underwater.

components.note: 汤 depicts hot water — its heat is strong enough to wipe out whatever it touches.
艹 (plant) — hot water 汤 wiping out plant life gave 荡 its meaning 'to wash away, to sweep clean.'
女 (woman) forms the left side of the character.
彐 depicts a broom — a woman holding a broom, a traditional image of housework, gave 妇 its meaning 'married woman, wife.'

example.hanzi: 那部小说描写了一个被称为荡妇的女人。
example.pinyin: nà bù xiǎoshuō miáoxiěle yī gè bèi chēngwéi dàngfù de nǚrén.
example.english: That novel depicts a woman who is called a slut.
example.fact: The historical "scarlet letter" punishment in colonial New England, made famous by Nathaniel Hawthorne's 1850 novel, required women convicted of certain sexual offenses to visibly wear a mark identifying their status, a legal practice that existed in some Puritan colonies well before the novel dramatized it.

components.note: 革 (leather) — 靴 (boots) were traditionally made of leather.
化 (huà) gives a sound only distantly related to xuē today, a connection that has faded over roughly three millennia of sound change.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 冬天穿这双靴子很暖和。
example.pinyin: dōngtiān chuān zhè shuāng xuēzi hěn nuǎnhuo.
example.english: Wearing these boots in winter is very warm.
example.fact: Cowboy boots developed their distinctive high heel not for fashion but for function. The raised heel keeps a rider's foot from sliding forward through the stirrup, an engineering solution that spread across cattle-ranching cultures in the American West during the 19th century.

components.note: 亻 (person) — the one settling somewhere.
主 (host, master) — the idea of a person settled in a place as if hosting it, giving 住 its meaning 'to live, reside, stay.'
夂 (a foot, to go) — 处 relates to arriving somewhere.
卜 (a mark or flag) — planting a marker after arriving gave 处 its meaning of 'a place' or 'to settle, deal with.'

example.hanzi: 他找到了一个便宜的住处。
example.pinyin: tā zhǎodàole yī gè piányi de zhùchù.
example.english: He found a cheap residence.
example.fact: Cappadocia in central Turkey contains entire underground residences and even multi-story cities carved directly into soft volcanic rock starting more than a thousand years ago. The largest, Derinkuyu, could shelter up to 20,000 people along with their livestock and food stores during times of invasion.

components.note: 女 (woman) — 始's meaning 'beginning' has been linked to the idea of the origin of life.
台 (tái) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shǐ.
纟 (thread) — 终 originally referred to the end of a woven thread, extended to mean 'end, final'
冬 (dōng) gives a loose sound connection to 终's reading zhōng

example.hanzi: 她始终相信自己能够成功。
example.pinyin: tā shǐzhōng xiāngxìn zìjǐ nénggòu chénggōng.
example.english: She always believed, from beginning to end, that she could succeed.
example.fact: The Great Wall of China was not built as a single continuous project from beginning to end but assembled and extended piecemeal by different dynasties over roughly two thousand years. The best-preserved sections visible today date mainly from the Ming dynasty's rebuilding efforts in the 14th through 17th centuries.

components.note: A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'
车 (cart) — 辆 is used to count vehicles, one cart at a time.
两 (two) — its use here, counting out two carts, is the visual root of 辆's job as a measure word for vehicles.

example.hanzi: 这条路上的车辆非常多。
example.pinyin: zhè tiáo lù shàng de chēliàng fēicháng duō.
example.english: There are a lot of vehicles on this road.
example.fact: Norway has the highest rate of electric vehicle adoption in the world, with battery-electric cars making up more than 90 percent of new vehicle sales by the mid-2020s, driven by heavy tax incentives and cheap hydroelectric power that keeps charging costs low.

components.note: A pictograph of rising flames — the source of 火's meaning 'fire.'
又 (hand, here standing in for 奚, part of the original character) — a simplified stroke that no longer pictures anything on its own.
鸟 (bird) — combined with the simplified left side, 鸡 names a specific 'kind of bird,' the chicken.

example.hanzi: 感恩节的时候人们会吃火鸡。
example.pinyin: gǎn'ēnjié de shíhou rénmen huì chī huǒjī.
example.english: People eat turkey during Thanksgiving.
example.fact: Despite its English name, the turkey bird has no biological connection to the country Turkey. It's a North American species domesticated by indigenous peoples in Mexico, and it picked up its confusing name in Europe because traders initially confused it with African guinea fowl imported through Turkish territory.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 打 relates to hitting or performing an action with the hand.
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — 打 is pronounced dǎ, a connection that has shifted in tone.
Depicts a person standing with legs crossed — the crossing shape gave 交 its meaning 'to intersect, exchange, hand over.'
辶 (to walk) — 道 relates to a path or road one walks along.
首 (shǒu) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer resembles dào, a reminder that sound components can drift after thousands of years of pronunciation change.

example.hanzi: 我经常和外国客户打交道。
example.pinyin: wǒ jīngcháng hé wàiguó kèhù dǎjiāodào.
example.english: I often have dealings with foreign clients.
example.fact: Diplomats posted abroad receive extensive briefings on local customs before having any official dealings with foreign governments, a practice formalized by the U.S. Foreign Service Institute's "area studies" training program established in the 1940s, which remains a model for diplomatic training worldwide.

components.note: 几 depicts a small low table or stool with legs — a simple domestic object.
一 (one) — relates to 百's meaning 'hundred,' a large round number built from 'one.'
白 (bái) gives a sound hint — 百 is pronounced bǎi, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 这次活动来了几百人。
example.pinyin: zhè cì huódòng láile jǐ bǎi rén.
example.english: Several hundred people came to this event.
example.fact: A group of starlings performing their famous swirling "murmuration" can number in the several hundred to several thousand birds. Physicists studying the phenomenon found each bird tracks only its seven nearest neighbors, a simple local rule that produces the mesmerizing, coordinated motion of the whole flock.

components.note: 辶 (to walk/move) — shows 过's core meaning of 'passing through' or 'crossing'
咼 (guō) gives a sound close to 过's reading guò; the simplified form 过 now uses 寸 in place of 咼, but the phonetic connection traces back to the traditional character 過

于 is an ancient character whose oracle-bone form has been interpreted as depicting breath or air curling upward; it was later borrowed purely for its sound to serve as the grammatical preposition 'at, in, than.'

example.hanzi: 他对这件事过于担心了。
example.pinyin: tā duì zhè jiàn shì guòyú dānxīnle.
example.english: He is excessively worried about this matter.
example.fact: The Yerkes-Dodson law, first proposed by psychologists in 1908, describes how performance improves with stress and arousal only up to a point. Beyond that point, excessive stress actually degrades performance, a curve now widely cited in sports psychology and workplace research.

components.note: 宀 (a roof, house) — 安 pictures shelter.
女 (woman) — a woman safely inside a house gave 安 its meaning 'peace' or 'safety.'
女 (woman) — 妮 names a girl or young woman.
尼 (ní) gives the sound — an exact match with 妮, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 安妮明天要去北京旅行。
example.pinyin: Ānní míngtiān yào qù Běijīng lǚxíng.
example.english: Annie is going to travel to Beijing tomorrow.
example.fact: The name Annie is a diminutive of Anne, ultimately derived from the Hebrew name Hannah, meaning "grace" or "favor." The same root lies behind names like Anna, Ann, and Nancy, which all trace back to the biblical figure Hannah in the Book of Samuel.

components.note: 贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 账 relates to money and financial records.
长 (zhǎng) gives a sound close to zhàng, sharing the same rhyme and initial.
户 (a simplified form of 戶) depicts a single door panel swinging on its hinge.

example.hanzi: 请检查一下你的银行账户。
example.pinyin: qǐng jiǎnchá yīxià nǐ de yínháng zhànghù.
example.english: Please check your bank account.
example.fact: The world's first ATM was installed outside a Barclays branch in Enfield, London, in 1967, dispensing cash to account holders who inserted a paper voucher rather than the plastic card used today. The voucher was radioactively marked so the machine could detect it, a security measure quickly abandoned for safety reasons.

components.note: 图 is the simplified form of 圖, which pictured a district's borders 啚 enclosed within a boundary 囗 — an old image of a map, giving 图 its meaning 'picture, chart, map.'
亻 (person) — relates to 像's meaning 'to resemble, be like; image, portrait,' comparing one person or thing to another.
象 (xiàng) gives the sound — 像 is also pronounced xiàng, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 这张图像的分辨率很高。
example.pinyin: zhè zhāng túxiàng de fēnbiànlǜ hěn gāo.
example.english: This image has a very high resolution.
example.fact: The first digital image ever scanned was a photograph of Russell Kirsch's infant son in 1957, captured at a resolution of just 176 by 176 pixels using a rotating drum scanner Kirsch built at the U.S. National Bureau of Standards, a milestone considered the birth of digital imaging.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 撒 describes scattering something by hand.
散 (to scatter, to disperse) — combined with the hand 扌, it gave 撒 its meaning 'to scatter, to release.'
日 (the sun) — rising above.
一 (a horizontal line) — the horizon, together giving 旦 its meaning 'dawn, daybreak.'

example.hanzi: 这部电影讲述了一个关于撒旦的故事。
example.pinyin: zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎngshùle yī gè guānyú Sādàn de gùshi.
example.english: This movie tells a story about Satan.
example.fact: The name "Satan" derives from a Hebrew word meaning "adversary" or "accuser," and in the earliest Hebrew scriptures it functioned more as a role or title, an accusing prosecutor figure in a heavenly court, rather than the singular personified embodiment of evil that later Christian theology developed.

components.note: 凡 (common/ordinary) — suggests something shared or held in common.
口 (mouth) — sharing a common mouth/voice with others gave 同 its meaning of 'same, together.'
亻 (person) — 伙 relates to people who share meals or work together.
火 (huǒ) gives the sound — an exact match with 伙's reading huǒ.

example.hanzi: 警方逮捕了他的同伙。
example.pinyin: jǐngfāng dàibǔle tā de tónghuǒ.
example.english: The police arrested his accomplice.
example.fact: Wolves hunting in packs coordinate with their fellow pack members using specific howl patterns that researchers have shown convey information about the group's location and readiness to hunt, effectively letting accomplices synchronize an ambush across long distances in dense terrain.

components.note: 走 (to walk, to run) — 赶 relates to pursuing or hurrying, both forms of movement.
干 (gān) gives a rhyme close to gǎn, with the tone shifted.
Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'

example.hanzi: 听到消息后，他立刻赶来了。
example.pinyin: tīngdào xiāoxi hòu, tā lìkè gǎnláile.
example.english: After hearing the news, he rushed over immediately.
example.fact: Emergency medical responders rushing to a cardiac arrest are trained around what's sometimes called the "golden ten minutes": brain damage from oxygen deprivation begins within about four to six minutes, which is why bystander CPR performed before paramedics arrive dramatically improves survival odds.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — 股 originally referred to the thigh, a part of the body
殳 (shū) gives a sound related to 股's reading gǔ, though the two have drifted apart over time
覀 here depicts rising flames.
示 (altar) — burning paper offerings over an altar, a traditional practice, gave 票 its meaning of a paper note, later 'ticket, banknote.'

example.hanzi: 他昨天买了一些股票。
example.pinyin: tā zuótiān mǎile yīxiē gǔpiào.
example.english: He bought some stocks yesterday.
example.fact: The Dutch East India Company, founded in 1602, issued the world's first publicly tradable stock, and its shares were bought and sold on what became the Amsterdam Stock Exchange, arguably the birthplace of the modern stock market, more than a century before the London or New York exchanges existed.

components.note: 三 (three lines) — represents stalks or ears of a plant.
丨 (a vertical stroke) — the stem holding them up, together picturing a plant heavy with grain, the source of 丰's meaning 'abundant, bountiful.'
宀 (roof) — 富 relates to a well-stocked household, prosperous under its own roof
畐 (fú) gives a sound close to 富's reading fù, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

example.hanzi: 这个地区的自然资源非常丰富。
example.pinyin: zhège dìqū de zìrán zīyuán fēicháng fēngfù.
example.english: This region's natural resources are very abundant.
example.fact: The Democratic Republic of the Congo holds some of the most abundant mineral reserves on Earth, including over half the world's known cobalt supply, an element now critical to manufacturing the lithium-ion batteries used in smartphones and electric vehicles.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 插 describes inserting or sticking something in by hand.
臿 (chā) gives the sound — an exact match with 插.
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.

example.hanzi: 别插手别人的私事。
example.pinyin: bié chāshǒu biérén de sīshì.
example.english: Don't meddle in other people's private affairs.
example.fact: The Prime Directive in the fictional "Star Trek" universe, a rule barring interference in the natural development of other civilizations, was directly inspired by real anthropological debates in the 1960s about whether contact with isolated human societies does more harm than good, a concern still actively discussed by anthropologists studying uncontacted peoples today.
